notes: Identity independently checked: title Implicit Theories of Intelligence Predict Achievement Across an Adolescent Transition: A Longitudinal Study and an Intervention; authors Lisa S. Blackwell, Kali H. Trzesniewski, Carol Sorich Dweck; Child Development, January/February 2007, Volume 78, Number 1, Pages 246–263. Wiley header identifies DOI 10.1111/j.1467-8624.2007.00995.x. This is a primary article with Study 1 methods/results, Study 2, references and appendices, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF supplied. Two tests match: canonical b = .17, t = 3.40, p < .05 controlling sixth-grade mathematics test scores; canonical b = .10, t = 2.50, p < .05 controlling first-term junior-high mathematics grades. The description and page locator do not select a covariate, so target_match remains null, coefficient and p remain null, confidence false. Both p bounds coincide but a unique same-test correspondence is unresolved. Canonical b does not establish requested unstandardised metric identity. Study 1 overall participant count is 373; Figure 2 explicitly reports N = 373 for a separate SEM process model. Neither establishes an explicit analytic N for the target HLM or endpoint regressions. Target-test exclusions are not specified. No N sum or df-based derivation performed. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
